findings.failure_path: An uninstall interrupted before public plugin/marketplace state was removed leaves a journal with trashPath+snapshot while `exactState(p.codexHome, null, false)` is false. Every subsequent doctor/install/update/uninstall now returns code 5 status "partial" from this new guard before any recovery work, and nothing in the diff can make public state absent (uninstall itself never reaches its removal step). The host is permanently wedged with trashed files unrestored. The new quarantine tests only inject `trash-unlink`, which fires after public removal, so they cannot observe this.
findings.smallest_fix: Only apply the absent-public-state precondition when the journal step indicates public removal already completed (e.g. after the plugin/marketplace removal step), and otherwise allow the existing resume/rollback path to run.

findings.failure_path: `continuation_authorization` previously required platform-authenticated human authority outside the candidate diff. The replacement lets the agent record `continuation_basis=existing-task-scope` in a caller-owned artifact it writes itself and open another bounded sequence. No cap on the number of sequences is stated and no validator checks the basis (validate_extraction_review_state.py gains only `source_refuted_findings`). Literal path skipping the gate: reach the 3-round cap -> write the checkpoint fields -> start sequence N+1, repeated indefinitely, with the gated party adjudicating its own authority.
findings.smallest_fix: State an explicit maximum number of inherited-authority sequences (or cumulative rounds) after which a human decision is required, and pin that bound in the closeout validator rather than in prose only.

findings.failure_path: `uninstall` only calls `checkHost` inside `if (existsSync(p.journal))`. With no pending journal and Codex public state unreadable (state-unknown) or the CLI missing, uninstall proceeds to remove managed data and host assets without any host guard, contradicting the stated contract that managed data is retained when public state is unknown. No test in the diff covers uninstall-without-journal under a broken host.
findings.smallest_fix: Hoist `const host = checkHost(p.codexHome)` above the journal check in `uninstall` and return the same 3/4 host-failure result when `!host.ok`, before any removal.

findings.failure_path: The new grade-walk requires probes `prd-continue-gate-refactor`, `prd-stop-gate-waiver`, `prd-stop-gate-scope`, `prd-continue-review-authority`, `prd-stop-review-budget`, `prd-stop-review-scope` and aborts ("cleanup probe missing") if absent. Those probes live in eval/body-compliance-eval.rb, which the profile places in the other partition. If this delivery partition lands or is CI-checked without that file, the test hard-fails; the combined manifest that would prevent split landing is admittedly not yet committed.
findings.smallest_fix: Commit the exact-coverage landing manifest covering both partitions before landing, or skip the new subset with an explicit reason when the eval file is absent.

findings.failure_path: "An explicit user request to release, or an explicitly release-scoped item in a user-approved plan, includes preparing the patch version ... no separate confirmation is needed" lets the agent classify a plan item as release-scoped and then bump versions and lockfiles unprompted. The only counterexample given ("a general mention of a future release") is also self-classified, so the confirmation gate is reachable-around by the gated party's own reading of the plan.
findings.smallest_fix: Require the release-scoped plan item to be quoted verbatim in the change record, and require confirmation when the item does not literally name a version bump.

concern_results.conclusion: Not clean. Host recovery: the new uninstall-resume precondition (`j.operation === "uninstall" && !exactState(p.codexHome, null, false)`) has no forward path when the interruption happened before public state was removed — every command that touches the journal then returns code 5 "partial" permanently; the supplied quarantine fixtures only inject `trash-unlink`, i.e. after public removal, so the wedge is untested. Valid-journal mutation results: the R1 disposition is right that journal() accepts the literal shape used in operations.test.mjs, so F1's premise fails; the new `details.hostFailure` assertions do exercise the host guard. Process-group isolation: interruption.test.mjs:138-143 does set detached:true and the timeout path kills the group, so F3's premise is refuted; the new early-exit branch, however, awaits close without a group kill and can leave the sleeping fake-codex child behind. Inherited task authority: the replacement of authenticated `continuation_authorization` with self-recorded `continuation_basis=existing-task-scope` removes the only non-self-adjudicated bound on further reviewer sequences; nothing in the diff caps sequences or is machine-checked (the new pins are grep text pins).

Containment evidence is partial. Journal/manifest byte-equality assertions in operations.test.mjs and quarantine-faults.test.mjs are real containment proof for the state-unknown/probe-failed paths, and the safety-refusal tests prove no host query on an unsafe home. But: uninstall with no pending journal still runs with no `checkHost` at all, so managed-data removal proceeds without the public-state guard the acceptance claims; the validator change adds `source_refuted_findings` as a completion basis that the implementer both supplies and adjudicates (validation explicitly proves only binding, not truth), i.e. the gated party self-adjudicates completion; and the delivery partition's test_body_compliance_grading.sh depends on probes in eval/body-compliance-eval.rb, which is in the other partition, with the combined manifest admittedly not yet committed.
